open_seated_dumbbell_press_b32f5163.positionDetail: Upright seat with a back support.
open_seated_dumbbell_press_b32f5163.rationale: A clear seated free-weight compound, useful for comparing supported pressing with the standing barbell press while keeping both arm paths visible.
movementSequence: Begin already seated against the back support, with two distinct dumbbells at shoulder height and palms facing forward.
Press both dumbbells upward together until they meet lightly at the top.
Pause briefly, then lower both dumbbells slowly to the same shoulder-height starting position.
setupOutsideClip: The catalog describes bringing the dumbbells from the thighs to the shoulders one at a time. Keep that setup in the text; the short motion clip starts after it.
formConstraints: Use a bench with a visible back support; do not substitute an unsupported stool or a standing press.
Keep hips and back supported, and the dumbbells distinct with stable closed grips.
Keep palms forward through the cycle; do not add Arnold-press wrist rotation or alternating arms.
The existing catalog says the dumbbells touch at the top; depict a gentle meeting without collision, fusion or a change of grip.

camera.view: Near-frontal view with a slight three-quarter offset so both forearms and the back support remain distinguishable.
camera.height: About the seated upper-chest height; avoid a low heroic angle.
camera.framing: Frame the supported pelvis through the complete overhead dumbbell range tightly. Include the seat and enough legs to establish seated support; use the setup still for the full feet-to-bench context.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: The arm paths and shoulder-height return should occupy the central image, with little empty studio above or beside them.
camera.secondaryStill: A closer front three-quarter shoulder-height start frame showing palms forward and two independent dumbbells.

open_seated_dumbbell_press_b32f5163.loopPolicy: A top hold is followed by a full return to the shoulder-height start; the same seated pose can loop.

counting.oneRepetition: One simultaneous press and controlled return of both dumbbells.
counting.sidePolicy: Bilateral repetitions; do not count the two arms separately.

rejectionCriteria: Back support disappears or hips lift off the seat
Weights merge, change shape, or collide through each other
One arm moves alone or grip rotates into another press variant
The return stops well above shoulder height
open_seated_dumbbell_press_b32f5163.muscleGuidePolicy: Catalog primary shoulders and secondary triceps. Use only credible visible regions or an adjacent legend; do not fake hidden triceps segmentation.

ex_seated_cable_row.positionDetail: Tall seated position on a dedicated low-cable row station, with feet braced and knees softly bent.
ex_seated_cable_row.rationale: Adds a seated horizontal pull with an unmistakable handle endpoint; the close view tests cable continuity and avoids hiding the action inside a large machine scene.
movementSequence: Begin seated tall with feet braced, knees softly bent and arms reaching forward to a taut low-cable handle.
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs while keeping the torso steady.
Reach forward under control to the same starting arm position without rounding or rocking the torso.
setupOutsideClip: Keep station setup and resistance selection in the text; no weight-stack adjustment is part of the motion clip.
formConstraints: Use the dedicated seated cable-row station named by the catalog.
Keep the handle attached to one taut cable aligned with the low pulley throughout.
Keep feet braced, knees softly bent, and hips on the seat.
Show the lower-rib endpoint clearly without leaning backward to manufacture extra travel.

camera.view: Close side view with a small turn toward the front, enough to separate the two hands and show the handle-to-lower-rib relationship.
camera.framing: Keep the torso, arms, handle travel, braced feet and immediate cable/low-pulley route. Omit the unrelated weight-stack tower and wide room.
mustRemainVisible: Taut cable and its immediate pulley route
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: The handle, elbows and steady trunk fill the frame; the pull endpoint must remain readable without zooming.
camera.secondaryStill: Close side start/end comparison of the handle at full reach and at the lower ribs, using the same camera.

ex_seated_cable_row.loopPolicy: Return to the initial reaching position with a short hold; no torso reset or cable slack.

counting.oneRepetition: One pull toward the lower ribs and controlled forward return.

rejectionCriteria: Row becomes a rocking rowing-machine stroke
Torso rounds or leans backward visibly
Handle approaches the upper chest or neck instead of the lower ribs
Cable detaches, passes through the body, or changes anchor
ex_seated_cable_row.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary upper back; secondary lats, biceps and forearms. The main back regions may be hidden in this camera, so prefer a legend or separately reviewed back-view still.

ex_lat_pulldown.positionDetail: Seated at a dedicated lat-pulldown station with the thighs secured by a pad.
ex_lat_pulldown.rationale: Adds a seated vertical pull and directly tests the visible upper-chest endpoint, supported thighs and continuous overhead cable path.
movementSequence: Begin with the thigh pad secured, torso mostly still and both hands gripping the overhead bar with arms extended.
Pull the bar down in front toward the upper chest.
Let the arms extend under control to return the bar overhead.
setupOutsideClip: Seat and thigh-pad adjustment remains in the Form text; the pad must already visibly secure the thighs in the motion frame.
formConstraints: Use a dedicated lat-pulldown station with an overhead cable, bar and thigh pad.
The bar travels in front of the face toward the upper chest, never behind the neck.
Keep the torso mostly still and hips seated; do not swing backward to create the pull.
The catalog does not set a precise grip width or require literal chest contact; choose one ordinary symmetric grip and keep it unchanged.

camera.view: Front three-quarter view with only a small side offset, keeping both elbows visible and the bar in front of the chest.
camera.framing: Crop around the complete overhead bar range down to the seat/thigh pad and knees. Include the immediate overhead cable route; keep the remote weight stack out of the composition.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: Use a torso-and-arm close framing; do not shrink the person to include the entire station.
camera.secondaryStill: Close oblique endpoint image showing the bar in front of the upper chest and the restrained torso.

ex_lat_pulldown.loopPolicy: End at the initial extended-arm position with a short stable hold.

counting.oneRepetition: One front pulldown and controlled overhead return.
counting.sidePolicy: Both arms pull the same bar together.

rejectionCriteria: Bar travels behind the head
Thighs leave the pad or hips leave the seat
Torso swings sharply or movement becomes a seated row
Cable disconnects or the bar merges through the head
ex_lat_pulldown.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary lats; secondary biceps and forearms. Do not paint lats onto the front chest because the camera cannot see their full region.

ex_leg_press.positionDetail: A supported reclined seat on a sled-style leg-press machine.
ex_leg_press.rationale: A seated lower-body compound with a different support and load path from squatting; close framing makes knee/hip motion and lower-back support observable.
movementSequence: Begin supported against the adjusted seat/back pad, with both feet on the sled platform and knees short of forceful lockout.
Lower the sled through a comfortable knee bend while the lower back remains supported.
Press the sled away under control to the same starting extension, without forcefully locking the knees.
setupOutsideClip: Seat adjustment and safe machine entry/exit are retained as text and setup context; do not animate an unlock mechanism whose design is not established.
formConstraints: Choose one coherent common sled machine and keep its rails, platform, seat and contact geometry fixed.
Both feet remain on the same rigid platform; both legs work together.
Keep the lower back and hips supported throughout; do not fold until the pelvis lifts.
Use a comfortable visible bend, without declaring one universal knee angle or depth.
Do not substitute the catalog's separate Smith-attachment vertical leg press.

camera.view: Near side view with a modest elevated three-quarter offset so both feet, the knees and the lower-back/back-pad contact can be distinguished.
camera.height: Near the seat/hip level, raised only enough to reveal the platform contact.
camera.framing: Frame the back pad, pelvis, complete legs, platform and short section of the working rails. Crop decorative machine frame and unused plate storage.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: The supported pelvis, knees and platform dominate; do not devote half the image to empty machine frame.
camera.secondaryStill: A closer lowered-sled frame that clearly shows supported hips and comfortable knee bend.

ex_leg_press.loopPolicy: Return to the initial non-forceful extension and hold without a machine reset.

counting.oneRepetition: One controlled sled lowering and press back to the starting extension.
counting.sidePolicy: Both legs move the same platform together.

catalogAmbiguities: The catalog specifies a sled and supported seat but not a machine brand, rail angle or foot placement width. The chosen machine is one illustration, not a universal setup specification.
rejectionCriteria: Seat or lower back loses support at the bottom
Feet slide or leave the platform
Sled floats, rotates, or leaves its rails
Knees snap backward into lockout
Machine becomes a Smith vertical press or one-leg variant
ex_leg_press.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary quadriceps; secondary glutes, hamstrings and calves. Use only visible regions; the seat obscures some posterior anatomy.

ex_machine_chest_press.positionDetail: Upright seated chest-press machine with back support.
ex_machine_chest_press.rationale: A seated horizontal push provides a useful controlled-machine comparison to Bench Press, with a closer view of elbow motion and chest-height handles.
movementSequence: Begin with the seat adjusted so the two handles align with the middle of the chest and the back is supported.
Press the handles forward together while retaining back support.
Return the handles toward the same chest-height starting position under control.
setupOutsideClip: Seat adjustment is shown by the resulting alignment and retained in text, rather than a separate animated adjustment procedure.
formConstraints: Use one coherent seated press mechanism with two stable handles; keep the hardware consistent through its arc.
The handles start around mid-chest height and remain attached to the machine.
Back and hips stay supported; do not lift or lean forward to finish the press.
Show elbow extension and return rather than a fly-like sweeping arm motion.

camera.view: Close side three-quarter view that separates both handles and shows the back touching the pad.
camera.framing: Keep the supported seat/pelvis, torso, head and complete handle/forearm travel. Limit the surrounding machine to the parts needed to explain the motion.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: Frame the chest, elbows and handle excursion much larger than the wide Bench pilot.
camera.secondaryStill: Close start-position image showing handle-to-mid-chest alignment and back support.

ex_machine_chest_press.loopPolicy: Return to the initial handle position and supported posture with a short hold.

counting.oneRepetition: One forward press and controlled return.

catalogAmbiguities: No exact machine linkage or grip is specified. Choose one ordinary seated press design and do not imply it fits every machine.
rejectionCriteria: Handles float or detach from the machine
Motion changes into a pec fly or overhead press
Back leaves the pad
Chest-height starting alignment is hidden or visibly wrong
ex_machine_chest_press.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary chest; secondary triceps and shoulders. Keep any masks separate from generation and aligned to this specific image.

ex_squat.positionDetail: Standing barbell back squat inside a rack with safeties.
ex_squat.rationale: Adds a foundational standing lower-body compound with simultaneous hip/knee motion and visible whole-foot support; contrasts directly with the seated leg press.
movementSequence: Begin standing with the bar securely across the upper back after setup, with rack safeties already positioned.
Brace and bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth.
Stand back up by pressing through the whole foot, returning to the initial stable posture.
setupOutsideClip: Setting the safeties and securing the bar across the upper back stay in the Form instructions. The short repetition begins after unracking.
formConstraints: Keep the bar across the upper back; do not turn the movement into a front squat or overhead squat.
Keep both feet grounded throughout, with coherent hip and knee bending.
Allow natural torso inclination while braced; do not force an artificially vertical torso or a fixed universal depth.
Rack and safeties remain stationary and do not intersect the bar path.

camera.view: Nearly side-on, with a small front offset to separate both knees and foot contacts.
camera.height: Around hip height with minimal perspective distortion.
camera.framing: Fit the whole head-to-foot body and bar through the complete squat, close to the frame edges with a small safety margin. Include only the immediately relevant rack uprights/safeties.
mustRemainVisible: Full comfortable bottom and standing return
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: The body should fill most of the portrait height; use no wide gym establishing shot.
camera.secondaryStill: Close side bottom-position image including the trunk, hips, knees and complete feet.

ex_squat.loopPolicy: Return to the same standing, supported bar position; do not rerack mid-clip.

counting.oneRepetition: One descent and return to standing.

rejectionCriteria: Heels lift or feet slide
Bar moves to the neck/front of shoulders
Depth is produced by obvious trunk collapse
Rack intersects the bar or body
Clip stops before the controlled standing return
ex_squat.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary quadriceps; secondary glutes, hamstrings and calves. Guides should follow the accepted pose, not impose an invented knee/toe line or fixed joint angle.

ex_deadlift.positionDetail: Standing barbell deadlift with a floor start and return.
ex_deadlift.rationale: Adds a standing hip-hinge lift and tests the bar remaining close to the legs; it provides a materially different compound pattern from squatting and pressing.
movementSequence: Begin with the bar over the middle of the feet, the hips hinged and knees bent to grip it, with the trunk braced.
Stand with the bar staying close to the legs.
Reverse the movement under control to lower the bar back to its starting floor position.
setupOutsideClip: Initial foot placement and grip setup are established in the starting frame and text; no stance change or grip transition is part of the repetition.
formConstraints: Use a conventional barbell floor deadlift, not a hanging Romanian-deadlift repetition.
Maintain one rigid bar, coherent closed grips, and a path close to the legs.
The trunk remains braced and both feet stay supported as hips and knees extend together.
Return the bar to the starting floor level without dropping it or bouncing into another rep.
Use plausible full-size plates so an artificially tiny plate does not silently change the starting height.

camera.view: Near side view with a slight front offset that reveals the bar-to-shin/thigh relationship and both foot contacts.
camera.height: Around hip height, not a floor-level dramatic view.
camera.framing: Keep the complete body and bar from floor start through standing. Leave minimal unused side space and enough headroom only for the standing endpoint.
mustRemainVisible: Bar staying close to shins and thighs
Both feet and plate floor contact
Standing endpoint without a backward lean
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: Make the bar-to-leg gap and hip movement large enough to judge; avoid a distant rack or room view.
camera.secondaryStill: Close side starting position with bar, feet, shins, hips and braced trunk clearly separated.

ex_deadlift.loopPolicy: End with the bar back at the floor start and a stable hold; no bounce or duplicated lift.

counting.oneRepetition: One lift to standing and controlled return of the bar to the starting floor position.
counting.sidePolicy: Both legs and both hands work together.

rejectionCriteria: Bar drifts visibly away from the legs
Lift begins from a standing hang rather than the selected floor start
Feet slide or plates pass through the floor
Torso visibly collapses or leans backward to finish
Grip, plate size or bar geometry changes
ex_deadlift.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary glutes; secondary hamstrings, quadriceps and lower back. No fabricated activation percentages or frame-by-frame heat changes.

ex_overhead_press.positionDetail: Standing barbell press from the front of the shoulders, with a rack used for setup.
ex_overhead_press.rationale: Adds a standing upper-body compound and a direct comparison with the supported seated dumbbell press; the key teaching point is overhead travel without a backward lean or leg drive.
movementSequence: Begin after stepping clear of the rack, holding a barbell at the front of the shoulders with a grip just outside shoulder width and the trunk braced.
Press overhead while keeping the ribs down and moving the head only enough to let the bar pass.
Lower the bar to the front of the shoulders without leaning back.
setupOutsideClip: Rack setup, unracking/stepping back and returning the bar to the rack after the set remain in the text. The clip demonstrates the repetition only.
formConstraints: Keep it a standing barbell press, not a seated press, behind-neck press, push press or jerk.
Keep the ribs controlled and avoid a visible backward lean.
The head makes only the small clearance movement needed for the bar; no clipping through the face.
Keep the bar rigid and both hands attached at the same grip width throughout.

camera.view: Side three-quarter view with a small front offset, chosen to make head clearance and trunk position visible.
camera.framing: Fit both feet through the full overhead bar position tightly. Keep both ends of the bar in frame, with a small margin above its maximum height.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: Use the portrait frame for the tall movement; omit a wide rack scene and unused floor.
camera.secondaryStill: Closer upper-body side starting frame showing the bar at the front shoulders and its route past the head.

ex_overhead_press.loopPolicy: Return to the same front-shoulder hold; no reracking or step change during the loop.

counting.oneRepetition: One overhead press and controlled return to the front shoulders.
counting.sidePolicy: Both arms press the same bar together.

rejectionCriteria: Knee dip or leg drive changes it into a push press
Bar passes behind the head or through the face
Torso leans backward substantially
Clip omits the shoulder-height return
ex_overhead_press.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary shoulders; secondary triceps and abdominals. Keep overlays separate and visibly schematic.

ex_lunge.positionDetail: Forward-travelling walking lunges, alternating legs, with bodyweight.
ex_lunge.rationale: Adds a travelling unilateral compound and tests a different counting rule; it must remain an actual walking lunge rather than a stationary split squat.
movementSequence: Step forward into a split stance and bend both knees to a comfortable depth.
Push through the front foot to travel forward into the next step, keeping the trunk tall.
Perform the next forward lunge with the opposite lead leg, then rise under control.
setupOutsideClip: Use a clear level floor and bodyweight for this demonstration. External load is optional in the catalog, so no dumbbells need to be added.
formConstraints: Travel forward and alternate lead legs; do not step backward to the same starting spot after each lunge.
Keep the trunk tall and each planted foot physically connected to the ground.
Both knees bend through a comfortable range, without an invented universal depth or joint angle.
Preserve limb identity and which foot is leading through both steps.

camera.view: Side view with a slight front offset so the lead/trailing knees and foot contacts stay distinct.
camera.height: About hip height, fixed for the clip.
camera.framing: Reserve only the corridor needed for two complete forward lunge steps. Keep the full body near the frame's vertical bounds and start near one side so it can advance without cropping.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: Use a close two-step corridor, not a distant gym walk; the body should still fill most of the frame height.
camera.secondaryStill: A close three-quarter split-stance frame showing which foot leads and both knees bent.

ex_lunge.loopPolicy: One-shot replay rather than an in-scene seamless loop. End where the person has travelled; never teleport or walk backward just to restore the first frame.

counting.oneRepetition: Each completed lunge step is one repetition.
counting.sidePolicy: The entered count is the total across both legs. The proposed two-step clip demonstrates two repetitions, not one.

rejectionCriteria: Motion becomes a stationary split squat or reverse lunge
The same lead leg repeats without alternation
The body slides, teleports or is cropped during forward travel
One two-step sequence is labelled as one repetition
ex_lunge.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary quadriceps; secondary glutes, hamstrings and calves. Any side labels must follow the actual lead leg, not a mirrored assumption.

cat_cal_low_stepup.positionDetail: Standing bodyweight step-up onto a low stable box, with a controlled return.
cat_cal_low_stepup.rationale: Adds a standing unilateral compound with a concrete apparatus contact and a per-lead-leg target; it exposes support and sequencing errors that a static image can miss.
movementSequence: Place one foot fully on a low stable box whose height permits stepping up without hopping.
Push through that foot until both feet are on the box.
Step the trailing foot down first, then bring the leading foot down to return to the starting floor stance under control.
setupOutsideClip: Use bodyweight and a low stable box. Do not add a rail, chair, strap or external weight to this no-extra-support variant.
formConstraints: Keep the lead foot fully supported on the box rather than perched on its edge.
The trailing foot joins the lead foot on top before descent.
The trailing foot descends first; maintain the same lead-leg identity for the full cycle.
The box stays stationary and rigid; no hopping or jumping.

camera.view: Side three-quarter view showing the near edge and top of the box, both feet, and the lead knee.
camera.height: Near hip height, slightly above the box top so foot placement can be seen.
camera.framing: Frame from the floor through the head at maximum step height. Keep the whole box and both feet visible, with little unused side space.
camera.phoneTeachingFocus: The feet, box and moving knee should remain large and unoccluded; do not sacrifice their visibility for a full room view.
camera.secondaryStill: A closer starting foot-on-box frame with full foot support and the low box height apparent.

cat_cal_low_stepup.loopPolicy: Begin with both feet on the floor, include placing the lead foot, and finish back on the floor. Keep the same lead leg for this cycle; show the other side as a separate clear cycle if needed.

counting.oneRepetition: One complete ascent and descent is one repetition.
counting.sidePolicy: Complete the entered target leading with each leg. The proposed single-lead clip is one repetition for that lead leg, not one repetition for each side.

rejectionCriteria: Movement becomes a jump or knee-raise variation
Only one foot reaches the top before descending
Leading foot steps down first
A foot clips through or hangs off the box
One cycle is presented as satisfying both sides
cat_cal_low_stepup.muscleGuidePolicy: Primary quadriceps; secondary glutes, hamstrings and calves. Use a separate legend unless the selected frame makes the intended region clearly visible.
